![title](73,51,556,79) # Ten identities worth knowing

![text](76,98,694,133) Each identity below is stated without proof. The numbers on the right are used for reference in the exercises that follow on the next page.

![text](76,156,468,171) The Gaussian integral over the whole real line:

![formula](403,181,928,227) $$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi}
\quad \text{(1)}
$$

![text](76,231,366,246) The sum of the reciprocal squares:

![formula](443,255,928,303) $$
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}
\quad \text{(2)}
$$

![text](76,307,379,322) Stirling's approximation for large $n$ :

![formula](413,333,928,361) $$
n! \sim \sqrt{2\pi n} \left(\frac{n}{e}\right)^n
\quad \text{(3)}
$$

![text](76,383,568,398) Cauchy's integral formula, for a point $a$ inside the contour:

![formula](403,409,928,448) $$
f(a) = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{\gamma} \frac{f(z)}{z - a} \, dz
\quad \text{(4)}
$$

![text](76,457,366,472) The gamma function, for $\operatorname{Re} z > 0$ :

![formula](383,483,928,529) $$
\Gamma(z) = \int_{0}^{\infty} t^{z-1} e^{-t} \, dt
\quad \text{(5)}
$$

![text](76,531,344,546) The Euler product, for $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$ :

![formula](363,557,928,605) $$
\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s} = \prod_{p} \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}}
\quad \text{(6)}
$$

![text](76,607,500,622) A Fourier series on the interval from minus pi to pi:

![formula](313,633,928,680) $$
f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (a_n \cos nx + b_n \sin nx)
\quad \text{(7)}
$$

![text](76,683,402,698) Differentiation under the integral sign:

![formula](337,709,928,757) $$
\frac{d}{dx} \int_{a}^{b} f(x, t) \, dt = \int_{a}^{b} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x, t) \, dt
\quad \text{(8)}
$$

![text](76,759,268,772) The binomial theorem:

![formula](369,783,928,831) $$
(x + y)^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} x^{n-k} y^k
\quad \text{(9)}
$$

![text](76,833,258,847) A limit that defines $e$ :

![formula](360,859,928,890) $$
e = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)^n \approx 2.71828
\quad \text{(10)}
$$

![title](153,31,843,62) # THE WESTERLY BULLETIN

![text](45,75,105,89) No. 318

![text](390,77,607,88) Thursday, the twelfth of March

![text](913,75,953,89) Free

![title](44,105,294,141) ## Harbour wall repairs to finish in May

![text](46,144,328,274) The council expects the last section of the harbour wall to be finished by the end of May, three weeks later than planned. The delay came from the storm in February, which washed away part of the temporary platform and a load of stone that was waiting to be placed. The footpath along the wall will stay closed until the work is done, and the ferry will keep using the north landing.

![title](44,294,293,329) ## Allotments: the waiting list reopens

![text](46,333,328,435) Residents who would like an allotment can add their names to the waiting list again from Monday. Twelve plots will become free in the autumn, when the new ground behind the sports field is divided. Applications are made on the form at the town hall, and the plots will be offered in the order the forms arrive.

![title](342,105,602,123) ## New hours at the library

![text](344,127,626,257) From the first of April the library will open at nine on weekdays and close at seven, an hour later than now. On Saturdays it will open from ten until four. The reading room upstairs will be available for groups who book it at least two days ahead, and the local history collection can now be searched from the terminals by the entrance as well as at the desk.

![title](343,279,575,296) ## Bus route 14 changes

![text](344,299,626,403) Route 14 will no longer run along Mill Street after the bridge there closes for inspection. Buses will use Station Road instead and stop outside the post office. The timetable stays the same, though the journey from the hospital to the market square may take two or three minutes longer at busy times.

![title](640,105,921,141) ## School choir wins regional prize

![text](642,144,922,274) Forty pupils from the upper school travelled to the regional festival last weekend and came back with first prize in the youth category. They sang three pieces, one of them written for the choir by its director. The judges praised the balance between the voices and the clarity of the words, and the choir has been invited to sing at the opening of the summer fair.

![title](641,296,915,327) ## Volunteers wanted for the beach clean

![text](642,333,922,435) The spring beach clean takes place on the second Sunday of the month, starting from the lifeboat station at ten. Gloves, bags and litter pickers are provided, and hot drinks will be served at noon. Last year more than ninety people took part and collected over four hundred kilograms of rubbish in two hours.

![title](60,38,543,57) # Conditions of hire: Ferrish Village Hall

![list](62,72,936,94)
1. These terms apply to every booking made through the hall's office, by telephone or in person. A booking is confirmed only when the deposit has been received and a written confirmation has been sent to the hirer.

![list](61,103,936,139)
2. The hirer must be at least eighteen years old and must be present for the whole of the booking. The hirer is responsible for the behaviour of every guest and for leaving the hall in the condition in which it was found, with chairs and tables returned to the store room and all rubbish removed.

![list](61,148,936,183)
3. The deposit is returned within fourteen days after the booking, less the cost of any cleaning, repair or replacement that the hall's caretaker considers necessary. Where that cost exceeds the deposit, the hirer will be invoiced for the difference and must pay it within thirty days.

![list](61,192,936,225)
4. Bookings cancelled more than twenty-eight days before the date receive a full refund of the deposit and of any fee paid. Bookings cancelled between twenty-eight and seven days before receive half of the fee; later cancellations receive no refund of the fee, though the deposit is returned in full.

![list](61,235,936,257)
5. Music must end by eleven in the evening and the hall must be empty by half past eleven. Amplified music is allowed only in the main room, at a volume that cannot be heard in the houses on the far side of the green.

![list](61,266,936,288)
6. Food may be served in the main room and the kitchen only. The kitchen's ovens and dishwasher may be used by the hirer after the caretaker has shown how they work; the hirer must not use any other appliance brought in from outside without written permission.

![list](61,297,936,319)
7. Decorations must not be fixed to the walls, the ceiling or the woodwork with nails, pins, tape or adhesive of any kind. Free-standing decorations are welcome. Candles and other open flames are not allowed anywhere in the building or in the garden.

![list](60,329,936,364)
8. The hall holds public liability insurance for its own activities only. Hirers running an event for paying guests, or bringing in performers, caterers or equipment hire firms, must hold their own insurance and show the certificate to the office at least seven days before the booking.

![list](61,372,936,395)
9. The office may cancel a booking if the hall becomes unusable through fire, flood, a failure of the heating in winter or any other cause outside its control. In that case the deposit and the fee are refunded in full, and the office has no further liability to the hirer.
